newsitem.title: USA: Avon reports higher first-quarter profit, stock down.
newsitem.headline: Avon reports higher first-quarter profit, stock down.

text.p: Avon Products Inc. announced a 10 percent rise in first-quarter profits Wednesday as strong international results helped outweigh a 1 percent drop in sales in the United States, its biggest market.
Stock in the world's leading direct seller of cosmetics and other beauty products dropped $1.875 to $57 in consolidated early afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange

Avon, famed for its "Avon ladies" who go door-to-door selling the company's products, earned to $41.3 million, or 31 cents a share, in line with analyst expectations. The earnings compared with profit of $37.7 million, or 28 cents a share, in the first quarter of 1996.
Sales rose 7 percent to $1.09 billion from $1.02 billion in the year-ago quarter.

In addition to the dip in sales, the U.S. operations had a 2 percent decline in pretax profit. The declines included a small loss, which had been expected, by the recently acquired Discovery Toys unit.

U.S. sales of jewelry and accessories and home entertainment products were down significantly due in part to a change in the pricing of "demonstration products" sold to sales representatives, the company said.
Pacific region sales rose almost 20 percent, with gains in all markets except Japan, where business was hurt by the strong U.S. dollar.
In local currency, Avon Japan posted a double-digit increase in sales, its first quarterly rise in to years. Profits from Japan are expected to improve later in the year, the company said.
European sales were especially strong in Britain and the emerging markets of Eastern Europe. Mexico had double-digit profit growth.
